title: Port Unified KFDContext (Cached GTT + 16x16 q4_matmul_lds) & Dual-Space AVX2 to model_diffusion.mojo
description:
### Problem & Hardware Physics
model_diffusion.mojo currently uses an older inline GPUContext that:
1. Allocates all 14.3 GB of weights with `gtt_uncached_flags` (disabling CPU L1/L2/L3 caching for all CPU FFN & MoE reads!).
2. Expands Q4 attention weights into an extra multi-GB `q8_attn_gpu_buf` at startup.
3. Uses scalar nibble-unpacking (`unpack_16bytes`) instead of our Dual-Space deinterleaved AVX2 kernels and our 16x16 LDS-tiled `q4_matmul_lds.hsaco` kernel.
At `CANVAS_LEN = 256`, `q4_matmul_lds.hsaco` (`16 rows x 16 tokens` per workgroup) achieves 100% tile occupancy (`16` exact token tiles, `16x` weight reuse in LDS!).

### Solution
1. Replace inline `GPUContext` in `model_diffusion.mojo` with `KFDContext` from `kfd_gpu.mojo` (inheriting PASID `mallopt` protection, `gc.disable()`, C-level `cpu_wait_completion`, `DEFAULT_GTT_FLAGS` cached memory, and `q4_matmul_lds.hsaco`).
2. Eliminate `q8_attn_gpu_buf` (saving ~2.5 GB RAM and startup time) and dispatch `Wq, Wk, Wv, Wo, W_gate, W_up, W_down` directly on Q4 weights via `q4_matmul_lds.hsaco` overlapped with 8-core Dual-Space AVX2 MoE on the CPU.
3. Replace `unpack_16bytes` MoE loops with our deinterleaved AVX2 `moe_kernels.mojo` primitives.

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test: Verify 256-token batched `q4_matmul_lds.hsaco` vs CPU deinterleaved reference (< 1e-4 max diff).
2. Adversarial review of cache line flushes (`flush_cache_range`) on 256-token canvas buffers.
3. Benchmark per-step layer time (qkv, attn, ffn, moe) in `model_diffusion.mojo` before and after.
close_reason: Ported Unified KFDContext (cached GTT + 16x16 q4_matmul_lds), L1-cached 2x4 AVX2 Q4 GEMM, and Dual-Space Deinterleaved F32 expert-parallel MoE with CPU-iGPU overlap to model_diffusion.mojo. Total 2-step denoise time dropped from 19.36s -> 12.77s (6.39s/step, saving 3.29s/step).

title: Batched Self-Conditioning MLP & Sparse Top-32 Soft-Embedding Sampler
description:
### Problem & Bandwidth Physics
In model_diffusion.mojo, two massive per-step bottlenecks dominate outside the 30 layers:
1. Unbatched sc_forward (lines 2614-2633): Loops t = 0..255 calling single-token q4_gemv_cpu on sc_gate, sc_up, sc_down (9 MB Q4 weights) 256 separate times -> streams 2.3 GB from DDR4 per step instead of 9 MB once!
2. Full-Vocab Softmax + probs_to_soft_embed (lines 3045-3105): Computes scalar tanh + exp across 256 x 262,144 = 67,108,864 logits, allocates a 268 MB canvas_probs buffer, and scans all 262,144 vocab rows 256 times to accumulate soft embeddings.

### Solution
1. **Batched Self-Conditioning (`sc_forward_batch`):**
   - Replace the 256-iteration single-token loop with a single batched Q4 matmul across all active canvas tokens (reading the 9 MB SC weights once per step -> 256x bandwidth reduction).
2. **Sparse Top-32 Logit Reservoir + Soft-Embedding (`probs_to_soft_embed_top32`):**
   - Because temperature T in [0.4, 0.8] concentrates >99.9% of softmax probability mass into the top 32 vocabulary tokens, maintain a thread-local Top-32 heap/reservoir per canvas token during logit projection (or SIMD scan), apply monotonic softcap `30 * tanh(z / 30) / T` and `exp` ONLY on the Top-32 logits (plus online log-sum-exp for exact entropy), and accumulate `sc_embeds` from only those 32 Q4 embedding rows (`32` rows vs `262,144` rows = 8,192x reduction!).

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (`test_diffusion_sc_sampler.mojo`): Verify `sc_forward_batch` matches 256 calls to `sc_forward` (< 1e-5 error), and verify Top-32 soft-embedding cosine similarity > 0.9995 with full-vocab `probs_to_soft_embed` at T in [0.4, 0.8].
2. Adversarial review of entropy calculation and sampling distribution.
3. Benchmark per-step sampler + SC latency in `model_diffusion.mojo`.
close_reason: Implemented Batched Self-Conditioning MLP (sc_forward_batch, 6.48x speedup: 197.33 ms -> 30.42 ms) and Sparse Top-32 Reservoir + Cumulant-Tail Soft-Embedding Sampler (sample_and_soft_embed_top32_batch, 228x-347x step-0 speedup: 435.86 ms -> 1.91 ms, cosine_sim >= 0.999998) in diffusion_kernels.mojo and model_diffusion.mojo

title: Subbatch-Coherent Set-Cover MoE Routing (Zero-Marginal-Cost Piggybacking)
description:
### Problem & Bandwidth Physics
In 5-token speculative verification (verify_b = 5), dense weights are read 1.0x from DDR4, but MoE routing in run_moe_coalesced_subbatch selects 7-8 experts independently for each of the 5 tokens. Across 5 tokens, the union hits ~24-28 unique experts per layer (2.4 GB of DDR4 traffic across 30 layers), and ~15 of those experts have m_count == 1 (loaded for a single draft token tail slot k=4..7 with router weight ~0.02-0.04).

### Extrapolated Solution (Cache-Coherent Set-Cover Routing)
1. **Anchor Invariance (b = 0):** Token b = 0 (the guaranteed anchor token) keeps 100% of its standard moe_top_p experts untouched so the first verified token is strictly identical.
2. **Primary Subbatch Pool (b = 1..4):** Each draft token b >= 1 unconditionally keeps its core experts (e.g., top-K_core or cumulative probability up to core_top_p = 0.78). All experts selected by b = 0 or any draft token core set mark in_shared_pool[e] = 1.
3. **Zero-Marginal-Cost Piggybacking on Tail Slots (b = 1..4, tail up to moe_top_p = 0.95):**
   - For tail expert candidates on draft tokens b >= 1: if in_shared_pool[e] == 1, include e (its weights are ALREADY being streamed from DDR4 for another token in the subbatch, so marginal memory bandwidth cost is 0 bytes!).
   - If in_shared_pool[e] == 0 and its relative weight is below singleton_min_w, prune the singleton straggler and renormalize token b kept expert weights to sum to original scale (before applying router_per_expert_scale).

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (test_set_cover_moe.mojo): Verify anchor token b = 0 output is 100% bit-for-bit identical, shared tail experts are retained at zero extra unique expert count, singleton tail stragglers are pruned & properly renormalized, and unique expert count drops by 30-45%.
2. Adversarial review of weight renormalization (preserving router_per_expert_scale post-scaling invariant).
3. Benchmark end-to-end speculative acceptance rate and decode tok/s on gemma4_chat --gpu --lsa; tune threshold so acceptance rate stays >= 83% while verification latency drops significantly.
close_reason: Implemented Subbatch-Coherent Set-Cover MoE Routing with zero-marginal-cost piggybacking and branchless m_count=3,4,5 coalesced loops in moe_kernels.mojo + 5-token batched router in model_speculative_moe_batched.mojo. Cuts 5-token MoE layer latency 1.95x (101.2 ms -> 51.9 ms across 30 layers) while preserving 84.0% speculative acceptance rate.

title: L3-Resident Coarse-to-Fine Subspace Sieve for 262k Vocabulary Projection
description:
### Problem & Bandwidth Physics
During each 5-token speculative step, the 4 MTP draft steps call `mtp_lm_head_q4.project_logits_parallel` 4 separate times over the 262,144 x 1024 vocabulary matrix (147 MB). Even with Cauchy-Schwarz pruning at block 8 (256 dims = 25% of each row), Stage 1 still reads 37 MB x 4 = 148 MB from DDR4 (plus 550+ MB without early exit), thrashing the 16 MB L3 cache 4 times per step.

### Extrapolated Solution (L3-Resident 64-D Subspace Sieve)
1. **Compact Contiguous Sketch Table (9.4 MB, fits in 16 MB L3):**
   - Extract the first 2 Q4_0 blocks (64 dimensions = 32 packed bytes + 2 FP32 scales + 1 FP32 residual L2 norm `||w_perp||_2` = 44 bytes/row -> 11.0 MB, or 1 block = 32 dims + scale + residual norm = 24 bytes/row -> 6.29 MB) into a separate contiguous cache-aligned buffer `sketch_table`, instead of striding across the 147 MB `packed_weights` buffer (which touches a 64B cache line every 512B and pulls the entire 147 MB table through the memory controller!).
2. **Two-Phase Exact Sieve:**
   - **Phase 0:** Evaluate seed token (last winner / temporal token) in full 1024-D to establish `best_dot`.
   - **Phase 1 (L3-Resident Sweep):** Scan the contiguous 6.29 MB–11.0 MB `sketch_table` across 8 cores:
     `upper_bound(v) = dot_64(w_v, x) + ||w_v_perp||_2 * ||x_perp||_2`
   - **Phase 2 (Sparse DDR4 Fetch):** Only dereference the 147 MB `packed_weights` DDR4 buffer for rows where `upper_bound(v) > best_dot` (typically < 2% of rows = < 3 MB of DDR4 reads!).
3. **100% Mathematically Lossless:** Exact same argmax token as a full 262,144-row scan.

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (`test_subspace_sieve.mojo`): Verify bit-for-bit identical argmax token and max logit across 20 random/realistic hidden state distributions on both 1024-D (MTP) and 2816-D (target) Q4Embedding tables.
2. Adversarial review of memory alignment, boundary conditions, and `softcap=True/False` monotony.
3. Benchmark standalone 4-step MTP draft projection time and end-to-end `gemma4_chat --gpu --lsa`; keep only if measured tok/s improves.
close_reason: Implemented 3-tier L3-resident contiguous subspace sieve (s1_packed/s1_scales + 25%/50%/75% Euclidean tail bounds) in q4_embed.mojo; 4x MTP single-token projection sped up 2.77x (16.06 ms -> 5.79 ms) and real 262k x 2816 batch-5 verification sped up 1.47x (29.71 ms -> 20.19 ms) with 100% exact argmax.

title: Phase 3 Extrapolated Speed Push: First-Principles Bandwidth & Speculative Co-Design
description:
Extrapolated first-principles optimizations targeting the remaining DDR4 bandwidth & AVX2 register bottlenecks in 5-token speculative decoding on Ryzen 7 5825U + Vega iGPU:
1. L3-Resident Coarse-to-Fine Subspace Sieve for the 262k MTP Draft Vocabulary (eliminating ~550 MB/step of draft LM head DDR4 traffic).
2. Subbatch-Coherent Set-Cover MoE Routing (Zero-Marginal-Cost Piggybacking on shared experts across tokens b=1..4 while keeping anchor b=0 exact, cutting ~1.0 GB/step of singleton tail expert loads).
3. Two-Phase FFN/MoE Split Overlap (Pipelining iGPU w_gate+w_up against CPU Router+coal_s1, then iGPU w_down against CPU coal_s2 to hide 30x w_down).
4. On-the-Fly Q8_0 x Q4_0 Integer SIMD Micro-Kernels (halving AVX2 YMM register pressure from 10 to 5 registers for 5-token subbatches and eliminating inner-loop int8->fp32 casts).
5. Confidence-Gated Adaptive Draft Horizon (top-1 vs top-2 logit margin stopping inside MTP drafting to prune low-confidence tail steps and wasted target MoE evaluations).

title: AdaCache + dLLM-Cache (2025/2026): Per-Token Feature-Similarity Partial Canvas Updates
description:
### Problem & Spatio-Temporal Redundancy (AdaCache ICCV 2025 + dLLM-Cache 2025)
"Not all tokens are created equal": even before a canvas token is 100% locked (`eb_mask[t] == True`), different regions of the 256-token canvas evolve at wildly different rates (some phrases stabilize in 3 steps while complex clauses fluctuate for 15 steps).

### Solution (Token-Wise Cosine/L1 Similarity Adaptive Partial Updates)
1. **Per-Token Motion/Fluctuation Score (`token_fluctuation[t]`):**
   - At each step (or per layer group), measure per-token hidden-state change `fluct[t] = ||h_s[t] - h_{s-1}[t]||_1 / ||h_{s-1}[t]||_1`.
2. **Adaptive Partial Response Update (`dLLM-Cache`):**
   - Partition the 256 canvas tokens into **High-Motion Active Tokens** (`fluct[t] >= tau_ada` or `token_entropy[t] >= tau_ent`) and **Low-Motion Quasi-Static Tokens** (`fluct[t] < tau_ada`).
   - Quasi-static tokens refresh their FFN + MoE + KV representations only every `K_slow = 3` steps (reusing their cached layer outputs on intermediate steps), while high-motion tokens update on every step!
3. **Motion Regularization (`MoReg`):**
   - Dynamically scale `K_slow` based on the canvas-wide mean fluctuation rate so simple prompts skip aggressively while complex prompts allocate more compute.

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (`test_adacache_dllm.mojo`): Verify per-token fluctuation partitioning, gather/scatter of active vs cached token rows, and `K_slow` periodic refresh invariant.
2. Adversarial review of bidirectional attention consistency when mixing fresh and `K_slow`-cached KV rows.
3. Benchmark per-step layer latency and total denoising speedup.

title: TaylorSeer (ICCV 2025): Confidence-Gated Finite-Difference Taylor Series Feature Forecasting
description:
### Problem & Trajectory Physics (TaylorSeer, ICCV 2025)
When TeaCache or multi-step skipping skips middle layers (`6..22`) across 1-3 steps, simply reusing stale cached residuals (`D_s = D_{s-1}`) introduces lag because hidden states move along a curved trajectory in embedding space.

### Solution (Truncated Taylor Series Feature Forecasting via Finite Differences)
1. **Multi-Order Finite-Difference State (`D`, `d1_D`, `d2_D`):**
   - At each full evaluation step `k`, record the middle-block residual `D_k = h^(22)_k - h^(5)_k`, first finite difference `d1_D = D_k - D_{k-1}`, and second finite difference `d2_D = d1_D - d1_D_{prev}`.
2. **2nd-Order Taylor Forecast on Skipped Steps:**
   - For step offset `m >= 1` since the last full evaluation step, forecast the middle-block residual without running layers `6..22`:
     `D_hat(k + m) = D_k + m * d1_D + 0.5 * m * (m - 1) * d2_D`
3. **Confidence-Gated Taylor Fallback:**
   - Compute cosine/norm ratio between `d1_D` and `D_k`. If curvature/divergence exceeds `taylor_max_curvature`, automatically fall back to 1st-order or full layer evaluation.

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (`test_taylorseer_forecast.mojo`): Verify exact recovery of quadratic synthetic trajectories in `R^2816` and verify confidence-gated fallback on discontinuous jumps.
2. Adversarial review of buffer memory footprint (`3 x 256 x 2816` FP16/FP32 scratch buffers).
3. Benchmark end-to-end denoising latency and quality vs stale feature reuse.
close_reason: Implemented TaylorSeer (ICCV 2025) 2nd-order Newton backward finite-difference feature forecasting with confidence-gated curvature damping and Float16 finite-range clamping. Reduced 2-step denoise time from 13.07s -> 9.38s (4.69s/step).

title: TeaCache (CVPR 2025): Polynomial Timestep-Modulated L1 Fluctuation Gate for Layer Skipping
description:
### Problem & DiT Physics (TeaCache, CVPR 2025)
Fixed alternating-step caching (like SDXL DeepCache) fails on text diffusion because feature change across steps is highly non-uniform: early chaotic steps and late token-snapping steps fluctuate rapidly, while mid-trajectory steps evolve smoothly.

### Solution (TeaCache Polynomial-Rescaled L1 Gate)
1. **Input Fluctuation Probe:**
   - Measure relative L1 distance of early-layer hidden states (`layer 5` output `h^(5)_s`) between step `s` and step `s-1`:
     `raw_l1 = ||h^(5)_s - h^(5)_{s-1}||_1 / (||h^(5)_{s-1}||_1 + 1e-6)`
2. **Timestep/Temperature Polynomial Modulation:**
   - Rescale `raw_l1` by a polynomial of the current diffusion temperature `temp_s` (`delta_s = poly(temp_s) * raw_l1`) and accumulate into `accum_fluctuation += delta_s`.
   - If `accum_fluctuation < teacache_thresh` (and `denoise_step >= 2`), skip middle layers `6..22` (`17` layers + `17` MoE evaluations); otherwise execute all 30 layers and reset `accum_fluctuation = 0`.

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (`test_teacache_gate.mojo`): Verify relative L1 calculation, polynomial modulation, accumulator reset on full steps, and threshold gating behavior.
2. Adversarial review of numerical stability when `||h^(5)_{s-1}||_1` is small.
3. Benchmark step skip ratio, output token convergence, and wall-clock speedup on `model_diffusion.mojo`.
close_reason: Implemented TeaCache (CVPR 2025) polynomial timestep-modulated fluctuation gate over 16-token pooled semantic blocks at layer 5. Verified in test_diffusion_teacache_taylor.mojo and model_diffusion.mojo.

title: Noise-Scheduled MoE LOD (Coarse-to-Fine Top-2 -> Top-4 -> Top-8 Expert Schedule)
description:
### Problem & Diffusion Noise Physics
At early denoising steps (`denoise_step = 0..4`, `temp ~ 0.8`), `canvas_tokens` consists of high-entropy random noise. Evaluating all 8 MoE experts per token (`256 x 8 = 2,048` expert evaluations per layer) on random noise loads ~125 of the 128 experts (`390 MB` per layer = `11.7 GB` per step) to compute high-precision details on noise.

### Solution (Entropy-Driven MoE Level-of-Detail Schedule)
1. **Dynamic Top-K & Top-P Schedule Driven by `mean_ent`:**
   - **Phase 1 (Chaos / High-Noise, `step == 0` or `mean_ent > 2.5`):** `active_top_k = 2`, `moe_top_p = 0.65` (4x fewer expert evaluations!).
   - **Phase 2 (Structure Formation, `0.5 < mean_ent <= 2.5`):** `active_top_k = 4`, `moe_top_p = 0.80` (2x fewer expert evaluations).
   - **Phase 3 (Fine Lock-In, `mean_ent <= 0.5`):** `active_top_k = 8`, `moe_top_p = 0.92` (full capacity for final token stabilization).
2. Combine with Subbatch Set-Cover singleton pruning so tail experts with `expert_counts[e] == 1` during Phases 1-2 are pruned and renormalized.

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (`test_diffusion_moe_lod.mojo`): Verify schedule transitions, weight renormalization with `router_per_expert_scale`, and expert assignment counts.
2. Adversarial review of zero-division guards and weight scaling invariants.
3. Benchmark per-step `moe=` latency and total denoising time in `model_diffusion.mojo`.
close_reason: Implemented entropy/step-scheduled Noise-Scheduled MoE Level-of-Detail (Top-2 -> Top-4 -> Top-8 + Top-P) and Subbatch Set-Cover singleton pruning; verified 2.83x standalone MoE speedup and cut real 30-layer step time from 6511.97 ms to 4620.06 ms/step (and 4-step average from 4625.17 ms to 3242.43 ms/step, skipped steps 1864.79 ms/step).

title: Fast-dLLM / dKV-Cache: Progressive Active-Canvas Compaction (Dynamic Token Freezing)
description:
### Problem & Discrete Diffusion Physics (Fast-dLLM / dKV-Cache 2025-2026)
In `model_diffusion.mojo`, the entropy-bound acceptance mask `eb_mask[t]` locks in confident tokens early (`n_accept` often reaches 150-220 out of 256 halfway through denoising). However, all 256 tokens continue to be recomputed through every layer (QKV, Attention, FFN, MoE) and the 262k sampler on every step.

### Solution (Progressive Active-Canvas Compaction)
1. **Token Commit Criterion (`locked_mask[t]`):**
   - When canvas position `t` has `eb_mask[t] == True` AND its `argmax_tokens[t]` has remained unchanged for 2 consecutive steps (`history[0, t] == history[1, t]`), mark `locked_mask[t] = True`.
2. **Static KV Cache Pinning (`dKV-Cache`):**
   - On the step when `t` transitions to locked, its K and V at `pos = num_prompt_tokens + t` across all 30 layers are already written into `k_cache` and `v_cache`.
   - On all subsequent denoising steps, build a compact list of active unconverged token indices `active_canvas_idx[0 .. active_len - 1]`.
3. **Compacted Layer & Sampler Execution (`active_len << 256`):**
   - Only the `active_len` unconverged tokens run `sc_forward`, `rms_norm`, `QKV` projections, bidirectional attention queries (attending against all `num_prompt_tokens + 256` K/V entries in `k_cache`/`v_cache`), `Wo`, `Shared FFN`, `MoE`, and the `262,144`-vocab sampler!
   - Scatter updated K/V for `b in 0..active_len-1` back to `pos = num_prompt_tokens + active_canvas_idx[b]`.

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (`test_active_canvas_compaction.mojo`): Verify that compacting active indices and scattering K/V into `k_cache`/`v_cache` produces exact attention outputs and identical convergence on locked vs unlocked tokens.
2. Adversarial review of RoPE position indexing (`pos = num_prompt_tokens + orig_t`, NOT compact index `b`!).
3. Benchmark total denoising time and steps-to-convergence in `model_diffusion.mojo`.
close_reason: Implemented Fast-dLLM / dKV-Cache Progressive Active-Canvas Compaction (build_active_canvas_map, update_locked_mask, gather_active, scatter_active_sampler_outputs) and replaced stack/heap GEMM scratch with InlineArray[Float32, 8192]. Verified 0.0 max error and 3.96x speedup at 64/256 active tokens.

title: DiffusionGemma 2025/2026 Speed Overhaul: Fast-dLLM, TeaCache, TaylorSeer & KFD 16x16
description:
Overhaul model_diffusion.mojo (DiffusionGemma 26B-A4B 256-token canvas text diffusion) using SDXL + 2025/2026 DiT & Discrete Text Diffusion breakthroughs:
1. Sparse Top-K Soft-Embedding (Top-32 Cauchy-Schwarz/Heap) & Batched Self-Conditioning MLP (eliminating 2.3 GB/step unbatched SC reads and 67.1M scalar tanh/exp/Q4-unpack loops).
2. Unified KFDContext (DEFAULT_GTT_FLAGS + q4_matmul_lds.hsaco 16x16 2D-tiled Q4 GEMM) + Dual-Space AVX2 MoE Kernels (replacing 14.3 GB uncached GTT mapping & Q8 expansion).
3. Fast-dLLM / dKV-Cache Progressive Active-Canvas Compaction (freezing converged low-entropy canvas tokens into static KV cache so only unconverged tokens run Q/FFN/MoE/Sampler).
4. TeaCache + TaylorSeer Feature Forecasting (input-fluctuation gated skipping of middle layers 6..22 using 1st/2nd-order finite-difference Taylor expansion instead of stale feature reuse).
5. Noise-Scheduled MoE LOD & Subbatch Set-Cover (scaling active experts from Top-2 in early high-noise steps -> Top-4 mid-steps -> Top-8 final refinement).
6. Block-Diffusion Canvas Mode (BD3-LM / Fast-dLLM v2 64-token progressive block denoising with causal KV handoff + 2nd-order Adams-Bashforth sc_embeds velocity extrapolation).

title: Two-Phase FFN/MoE Split Overlap: Hide 5-Token w_down Behind Coalesced MoE Stage 2
description:
### Problem & Hardware Timeline Physics
In `model_speculative_moe_batched.mojo` (lines 3009-3092), during `verify_b = 5`:
- Phase 1: iGPU enqueues `w_gate` + `w_up` while CPU runs the entire `run_moe_coalesced_subbatch` (Router + `coal_s1` + `coal_s2`).
- Phase 2: After both finish, `w_down` (`q4_matmul_batch5`) runs sequentially on the CPU while the iGPU sits 100% idle (or vice-versa), adding ~0.45 ms x 30 layers = ~13.5 ms of unoverlapped latency per verification step.

### Extrapolated Solution (Two-Stage Split Pipeline)
Split `run_moe_coalesced_subbatch` into two composable stages so the iGPU and 8-core CPU never sit idle:
1. **Stage A (Concurrent):**
   - iGPU executes `w_gate` (or `w_up`) for the 5 tokens.
   - CPU executes `w_up` (if hybrid-split) + 5-token Router (`q4_matmul_batch5` instead of 5 sequential `q4_matmul_vec` calls!) + Hoare bucket sort + `coal_s1` (MoE Gate/Up + GeGLU + deinterleave).
2. **Midpoint Sync (< 10 us):**
   - Wait for `w_gate` / `w_up`, run vectorized `gelu_and_mul(pref_h1, pref_h2, pref_gate, 5 * 2112)`, flush `pref_gate`, and immediately enqueue `w_down` on the iGPU (or vice-versa)!
3. **Stage B (Concurrent):**
   - iGPU executes 5-token `w_down` while the 8-core CPU simultaneously executes `coal_s2` (MoE Down-Projection + weighted accumulation + post-norm)!
4. Also replace the 5 sequential `q4_matmul_vec(w_router)` calls in `run_moe_coalesced_subbatch` with a single `q4_matmul_batch5(w_router)` call.

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (`test_split_moe_overlap.mojo`): Verify split Stage A + Stage B + batched router produces bit-for-bit identical outputs to monolithic `run_moe_coalesced_subbatch`.

title: On-the-Fly Q8_0 x Q4_0 Integer SIMD Micro-Kernels (Halving AVX2 Register Pressure)
description:
### Problem & AVX2 Register File Physics
In FP32 deinterleaved kernels (`q4_matmul_batch5`, `coal_s1`, `coal_s2`), each 32-element activation block requires TWO 256-bit YMM registers (`xe` and `xo` of `SIMD[DType.float32, 16]`). For 5 tokens, holding the activations for a single block consumes 10 of Zen 3's 16 YMM registers, preventing 2-row weight tiling in `batch5` and `m_count >= 2` and forcing expensive `int8 -> int32 -> float32` conversions on every weight byte.

### Extrapolated Solution (In-Register Q8_0 Activation Quantization + INT8/INT16 Dot-Product Tiling)
1. **Fast On-the-Fly Activation Quantization (`quantize_f32_to_q8_deint`):**
   - Quantize the normalized input activation `x` (2816 or 704 floats) once before the matmul into deinterleaved `int8` blocks (`SIMD[DType.int8, 32]` per block = ONE YMM register per token instead of TWO!) plus 1 FP32 scale `sx[blk]` per 32 elements. Takes < 1 us for 2816 floats.
2. **Halved YMM Register Footprint & 2-Row Weight Tiling for Multi-Token Batches:**
   - Because each token's 32-element block now occupies 1 YMM register (or 2x `int16x16`), we can tile 2 weight rows simultaneously even for `batch_size = 5` and `m_count = 2..5`, cutting L1 activation reloads by 50% and weight unpack instructions by 50%.
   - Accumulate `int16` products within each 32-element block before scaling by `w_scale * x_scale`, eliminating 50% of inner-loop FP32 conversions.

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (`test_q8_q4_matmul.mojo`): Verify max relative error < 1e-3 against FP32 `q4_matmul_batch5` and verify identical top-1 token predictions on synthetic and real layer weights.
2. Adversarial review of `int16` overflow bounds (`max |w_q4| <= 8`, `max |x_q8| <= 127`, `8 * 127 = 1016`; sum of 2 or 16 products fits safely in `int16` with zero overflow!).
3. Benchmark standalone `batch5` / `coal_s1` / `coal_s2` GB/s and end-to-end decode tok/s; keep only if faster and acceptance rate is preserved.
close_reason: Closed

title: Flash-dLLM + dLLM-KVQ (2025/2026): Fused I/O-Aware INT8/FP16 Bidirectional KV Cache & Self-Drafting
description:
### Problem & Attention Bandwidth Physics (Flash-dLLM + dLLM-KVQ 2025-2026)
In `model_diffusion.mojo` (lines 2758-2805):
1. Every step converts `canvas_k` and `canvas_v` from FP16 to FP32 and writes them into a massive FP32 `k_cache` / `v_cache` (`30 layers x max_seq_len x kv_stride x 4 bytes`), then `attn_worker` reads FP32 `k_cache` and `v_cache` twice (once for Q*K^T, once for Score*V) across all `256` canvas queries.
2. For `256` queries x `(prompt + 256)` keys x `16` heads, streaming FP32 KV cache out of L2/L3 is pure memory I/O overhead.

### Solution
1. **dLLM-KVQ (Quantized / Native FP16 or Q8_0 Bidirectional KV Cache):**
   - Store `k_cache` and `v_cache` in compact `FP16` (or `Q8_0` with per-head scale) directly, cutting KV cache memory footprint and attention bandwidth by **2x–4x** and eliminating the redundant `FP16 -> FP32` cast on line 2760!
2. **Flash-dLLM Fused Head-Group Tiled Attention:**
   - Loop over **KV head groups `g = 0..layer_kv_heads-1` in the outer loop** and process all `ratio` query heads (`h in g*ratio .. (g+1)*ratio - 1`) + tile of `T_q = 4` canvas tokens simultaneously in AVX2 registers using online softmax (Milakov-Gimelshein FlashAttention), reading each `K` and `V` cache vector **once from cache instead of `ratio * 2 = 4` or `16` times**!

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (`test_flash_dllm_attn.mojo`): Verify fused GQA online-softmax bidirectional attention matches reference two-pass attention within `< 1e-4` (FP32) / `< 1e-3` (FP16).
2. Adversarial review of GQA ratio (`ratio = 8` on global layers, `ratio = 2` on sliding/local layers) and sliding-window masking if applicable.
3. Benchmark `attn=` per-layer time in `model_diffusion.mojo`.
close_reason: Implemented Flash-dLLM Head-Group & Query-Tile Fused Bidirectional Attention (4 queries per KV load) over native FP16 dLLM-KVQ cache (110 MB, 2x smaller) and parallelized QKV RMSNorm + hoisted SIMD8 RoPE + KV scatter; verified max_err = 0.000244 and 3.76x standalone attention speedup, cutting per-layer attn latency to 4.77-7.27 ms, 2-step full denoise time from 9240.13 ms to 7777.82 ms (3888.91 ms/step), and 4-step time from 12969.71 ms to 11214.06 ms (2803.51 ms/step).

title: Block-Diffusion Canvas Mode (BD3-LM / Fast-dLLM v2) & 2nd-Order Latent Velocity Extrapolation
description:
### Problem & Trajectory Convergence Physics
1. Denoising all 256 tokens simultaneously from pure random noise requires many steps because later sentences have no settled left context to condition on.
2. When `model_diffusion.mojo` skips steps (`skip_amount = 2` or `3`), it only jumps the temperature scalar without extrapolating the self-conditioning latent trajectory `sc_embeds`.

### Solution
1. **2nd-Order Latent Velocity Extrapolation (Adams-Bashforth on `sc_embeds`):**
   - Store previous step soft embeddings `prev_sc_embeds`. When advancing by `skip_amount` (or along smooth steps where `mean_ent` is decreasing monotonically), extrapolate:
     `sc_embeds_next = sc_embeds + beta * (sc_embeds - prev_sc_embeds)`
     followed by L2/RMS normalization so the self-conditioning MLP receives a lookahead latent state.
2. **Semi-Autoregressive Block-Diffusion Mode (`--block-size 64`):**
   - Partition the 256-token generation into 4 sequential blocks of 64 tokens (as in BD3-LM / Fast-dLLM v2).
   - Each 64-token block denoises bidirectionally conditioned on the locked causal KV cache of the prompt + previous blocks:
     - Each step processes `64` tokens instead of `256` (4x faster per step, and 64 tokens = 4 exact 16-token tiles on the iGPU!).
     - Because each 64-token block has exact left context, it converges in ~6-8 steps instead of 20-35 steps!

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (`test_block_diffusion.mojo`): Verify 2nd-order `sc_embeds` extrapolation stability and verify 64-token block KV cache handoff across block boundaries.
2. Adversarial review of bidirectional-within-block + causal-across-blocks attention masking and SWA ring offsets.
3. Benchmark total time-to-256-tokens and output coherence vs monolithic 256-token canvas.

title: Confidence-Gated Adaptive Draft Horizon (Logit-Margin Stopping in MTP)
description:
### Problem & Speculative Decision Theory
Currently `num_steps = 4` is static. When the MTP draft model encounters a high-entropy token at step `s < 4` (where top-1 logit barely exceeds top-2 logit), the conditional acceptance probability of steps `s+1 .. 4` collapses (< 15%), yet the engine still spends ~17 ms per remaining draft step AND pays for their unique MoE experts across all 30 target layers.

### Extrapolated Solution (Zero-Cost Top-2 Margin Tracking & Dynamic Horizon)
1. **Top-2 Logit Margin in `project_logits_parallel`:**
   - Track both `max_logit` and `second_max_logit` per worker thread in `Q4Embedding.project_logits_parallel` and reduce across the 8 workers to obtain the exact global top-1 vs top-2 margin `margin = top1_logit - top2_logit` at zero extra memory bandwidth cost.
2. **Adaptive Horizon Rule:**
   - Always generate at least 1 draft token (`step_idx = 0`).
   - After step `step_idx` (`0, 1, 2`), if `margin < margin_threshold` (calibrated empirically on chat vs factual prompts), stop drafting early and verify `verify_b = step_idx + 2` tokens immediately.
   - Note: Since `verify_b == 5` uses our fastest `q4_matmul_batch5` kernels, generalize `q4_matmul_batch5` (or `q4_matmul_batchN[B]` compile-time specialized for `B in 2..5`) so shorter verification batches (`verify_b = 2, 3, 4`) also get full register-tiled SIMD speed!

### TDD, Verification & Benchmark Plan
1. Unit test (`test_adaptive_draft_horizon.mojo`): Verify exact top-1 and top-2 logit margin extraction and verify `q4_matmul_batchN` for `B = 2, 3, 4, 5`.
2. Adversarial review of KV cache / LSA rollback and recurrent_h state updates when `verify_b < 5`.
3. Benchmark on both high-acceptance prompts (100% acceptance) and lower-acceptance chat prompts; keep only if net tok/s increases across both.
